title: Coda launch timetable and quietwatch journal
content:
Purpose:
This is the working timetable + 'quietwatch' journal for the Coda launch window. The doc is intentionally tactical: exactly-timed handoffs, telemetry spotchecks, and short-form release notes we can paste into customer-facing channels. Use this as the single source for the 48h rollout runway and the first 72h stabilization watch log.

Launch objectives:
- Deploy coda-release v2.1.0 to hosted API and Dedicated staging pools with canary traffic split.
- Verify latency SLOs (p50 < 80ms p95 < 220ms for text-generation endpoints) and reduce token unit cost variance <= 8%.
- No customer-facing errors > 0.5% sustained for 30m.

High-level rollout plan (summary):
- T-48h: Preflight, smoke/test deploy to staging, compare metrics against baseline.
- T-6h: Dry-run deploy to a small internal cohort, telemetry baseline capture.
- T0: Canary (1%) to US region for 1 hour, progressive ramp to 10% at T+2h, 50% at T+6h, full at T+24h if green.
- T+72h: Post-rollout stabilization completed; quick retro and tag release notes final.

Day-by-day timetable (local times UTC):
- Day -2 (2026-03-12) 09:00: Preflight checklist complete (see checklist). 14:00: Staging smoke run, perf benchmark. 18:00: Release notes draft ready for review.
- Day -1 (2026-03-13) 08:00: Dry-run to internal cohort (canary-internal). 11:00: Ops handoff meeting (15m). 13:00: Final infra capacity check, GPU pool headroom validated. 17:00: Quietwatch roster published.
- Day 0 (2026-03-14) 07:00: Final freeze, no non-essential commits. 09:00: Canary deploy 1% (US only) — monitor 60m. 10:00: Canary review: run spotchecks, if green -> ramp to 10%. 12:00: 10% steady-state review. 14:00: Ramp to 50% conditional. 18:00: Nightly stabilization pass and operator notes.
- Day +1 (2026-03-15) 09:00: 100% rollout check (if conditions met). 13:00: Business owner post-deploy summary. 17:00: Quietwatch handover to next shift.
- Day +3 (2026-03-17) 12:00: Final retro, consolidate telemetry regressions and finalize release notes for external publication.

Preflight checklist (T-48h -> T-0) — quick ticks for leads:
- [ ] Code freeze confirmed and branch locked.
- [ ] Infra runbook updated with new service names and manifests.
- [ ] Canaries defined (1%, 10%, 50%).
- [ ] Canary criteria documented: latency p95 <= +20% vs baseline, error rate increase <= +0.3 percentage points.
- [ ] Smoke tests: tokenization, kv-cache warmup, streaming disconnect/reconnect flows.
- [ ] Load test: 30m ramp in staging at 2x expected peak to verify autoscaler behavior.
- [ ] TFLOPS and GPU memory checks for quantized model path.
- [ ] Rollback artifact ready (image + infra template + db-migration-reverse).
- [ ] Customer communications draft (support + sales slack snippets).
- [ ] Pager rotas confirmed for Quietwatch.

Quietwatch journal (shift-by-shift shorthand) — template entries to fill during watch:
- Shift: 09:00–17:00
  - Lead: Maya Singh (primary) / Liam Ortega (backup)
  - Check-in cadence: every 30m first 3 hours of ramp, hourly afterwards while steady.
  - Quickchecks: generation latency, model-cpu/ram, GPU utilization, queue length, failed-inference-rate, auth errors.
  - Notable signals to record: sudden p95 jump, tail latency without concurrency change, error clusters with same stack traces.
  - Action taken: (brief) e.g., scaled pool by +2 nodes, rolled back worker-type, cleared KV cache priming.

Smoke test list (scripts + expected):
- /scripts/smoke/gen-basic.sh -> returns 200 + sample tokens in < 200ms (p50).
- /scripts/smoke/stream-reconnect.py -> streaming reconnect resilience within 3 retries max.
- embed-checker.sh -> embedding similarity median diff <= 0.03 vs baseline.
- kv-warmup.sh -> cache hit rate >= 65% after 10k priming tokens.

Telemetry spotchecks and queries (ops quickcopy):
- Latency: SELECT p50, p95, p99 FROM infra.latencies WHERE service='coda' AND region='us' GROUP BY 5m
- Errors: count(status >= 500) by endpoint over 5m windows -> alert if > 0.5% sustained 30m
- Cost/unit: per_token_cost rolling 1h -> alert if > baseline * 1.12
- Queue: request_queue_depth -> alert if > 8 per worker for > 10m
- Model routing: ratio(local_quantized, remote_standard) -> log deviations > 10% from expected routing weights

Escalation & rollback criteria (short):
- Immediate rollback if:
  - sustained customer-facing errors > 1% for 15m OR
  - p95 latency > 3x baseline for 30m AND customer-impacting errors present.
- Partial rollback (back off to previous variant) if:
  - cost/unit increases > 25% without latency improvement OR
  - specific endpoint shows > 2x error rate compared to baseline.
- Escalation ladder: Shift lead -> Eng on-call -> SRE -> Product owner -> CTO if multi-region outage.

Communication plan snippets (paste-ready):
- Internal short update (for #release-watch): "Canary 1% live US — latency p95 180ms (baseline 160ms), errors 0.12% — green under canary criteria. Next: ramp to 10% at 10:15 UTC unless metric drift."
- Customer-facing blurb (support template): "We’ve deployed a minor performance and routing update to the inference platform. Most customers will see no change; if you observe degraded latency or increased errors please open ticket JIRA-RELEASE-789 and ping #support."

Draft release notes (to be polished post-retro):
- Coda v2.1.0 — rolling launch notes (draft):
  - Improvements: smarter kernel selection for quantized LLMs; average 7–12% token cost reduction in typical chat traffic (experiment-dependent).
  - Fixes: fixed a rare auth token renewal race causing transient 401s under heavy burst (jira: JIRA-RELEASE-789).
  - Migration notes: dedicated clients with manual model pinning should re-verify any pinned variants; default routing will prefer local quantized variants where available.
  - Known issues: small subset of legacy clients may see slightly higher memory pressure when using long-context sessions (workaround: reduce context or switch to non-quantized variant).

Post-deploy stabilization checklist (T+24 -> T+72):
- [ ] Consolidate 24h telemetry and compare to baseline; log any persistent regressions.
- [ ] Run golden prompt regression suite (10k prompts) — flag delta > 1% for manual eval.
- [ ] Finalize and publish release notes.
- [ ] Capture followups as Jira tickets and assign owners.

Open items before T0:
- (Maya) finalize customer blurb and get legal ok for the phrasing on model routing (due 2026-03-13 16:00).
- (Liam) validate feature-flag gating for fallback model in dedicated pools (due 2026-03-13 12:00).
- (Zoe) confirm observability retention config will capture 5m histograms for 72h (due 2026-03-13 18:00).

Notes & appendix (working):
- Keep an eye on the autoscaler SLOs — the new quantized path reduces per-token compute but can change concurrency characteristics; watch queue depth especially when ramping.
- If anomalies tie to a single model shard, prefer routing fallback to a different shard variant before a full rollback.
- This doc will be renamed and folded into the release-conductor binder once we finalize the post-mortem.

Quick log sample (fill during watch):
- 2026-03-14 09:25 UTC: Canary 1% live. p95 172ms, errors 0.08%. Action: no-op.
- 2026-03-14 10:05 UTC: p95 uptick 210ms correlated with increased queue depth. Action: added +1 worker in us-west, queue depth reduced to 3.
- 2026-03-14 11:20 UTC: A single endpoint /v1/rewrite showed 1.2% 500s for 10m, stack trace points to weight-load NPE. Action: route /v1/rewrite to previous variant, investigate.

If anything in here is unclear or you need different formatting (hand-off checklist vs. field journal vs. publishable release notes), flag in comments below and I’ll split into separate docs.

-- Maya
